source_meta.name: Urban Institute — State of the Safety Net 2025
source_meta.fetch_notes: apps.urban.org accepts curl with a browser User-Agent; datacatalog.urban.org returns 403.

model.name: ATTIS
model.method: Simulates program eligibility on pooled 2022+2023 ACS (2.7M households, adjusted to 2023). Participation rate = actual administrative caseload / simulated eligible count; the numerator is admin data, not simulation. Estimates refer to the average month of 2023.

source_meta.funders_note: Funders include the Pritzker Children's Initiative (also a PolicyEngine funder), Annie E. Casey, and Packard.
source_meta.diagnosis_upstream: ATTIS is closed-source; divergence diagnoses classified as external-model issues become a comparison memo, not an upstream PR.

period-vintage.text: PolicyEngine values are annual 2024 on the certified Populace artifact; Urban values are average-month 2023. Level differences partly reflect period and vintage, not only model differences.

participation-numerator.text: Urban's participation numerator is the actual administrative caseload divided by ATTIS-simulated eligibles. PolicyEngine's is simulated participation (seeded take-up flags + calibrated weights); for count-targeted programs (SNAP, SSI) the numerator is disciplined by the same class of admin counts, so convergence there is partly by construction.

snap-bbce.text: PolicyEngine's is_snap_eligible includes the full eligibility battery including BBCE categorical eligibility, matching Urban's denominator concept.
snap-bbce.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §2; engine metadata for is_snap_eligible in data/pe/pe_meta.json

ssi-payable-denominator.text: PolicyEngine's native is_ssi_eligible is explicitly 'without income test' — broader than Urban's payable concept. The scorecard instead uses adults with SSI amount > 0 under forced take-up (fullpart run) as the payable denominator, approximating Urban's concept. Child SSI is excluded (Urban's universe is adults 18+).
ssi-payable-denominator.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §2, §7 item 6; engine metadata for is_ssi_eligible; construction measured in data/pe/pe_metrics.json (run=fullpart_urban6)

tanf-payable-denominator.text: PolicyEngine has no national income-tested TANF eligibility variable (state-by-state machinery only). The scorecard uses persons in units where TANF pays > 0 under forced take-up as the income-eligible counterpart. TANF dollars on Build P miss the ACF admin total by −36%, so treat TANF comparisons as provisional.

tanf-ssf.text: Urban publishes family-level TANF participation with and without solely-state-funded (SSF) programs. PolicyEngine's TANF models the assistance-unit program without an SSF distinction; family-unit rows are not yet computed.

wic-children-only.text: Both sides count children ages 0–4 only; PolicyEngine's WIC eligibility also covers pregnant/postpartum women, excluded here by the age cut on both eligibility and participation.

wic-untargeted.text: WIC has zero calibration targets on Build P; the seeded legacy gate floats free. The close match to Urban's national rate (52.8% vs 53.5% in the replication assessment) is coincidence, not anchoring — FNS WIC targets are on the build list.

wic-infant-state-geography.text: Populace's national-default state geography has known 2–3x errors for infants in some states (e.g. CA hot, MI cold). State-level infant WIC rows carry that uncertainty.

eitc-forced-claims-denominator.text: PolicyEngine's eligible counterpart is tax units with EITC > 0 under forced take-up. Baseline EITC claims are SOI-targeted and include erroneous claims — nationally, claims (≈23.7M) exceed Urban's simulated eligibles (18.4M), one reason Urban publishes no EITC participation rate.

ctc-claims-calibrated.text: Build P stores no CTC take-up flag; refundable CTC > 0 is the formula outcome with claims and dollars calibrated to SOI. The count is closer to 'claims' than to a pure eligibility simulation.
ctc-claims-calibrated.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §3, §5; data/pe/pe_meta.json (no takes_up flag for CTC among stored inputs)

housing-ami-and-unit.text: PolicyEngine's housing eligibility is current recipient OR renter at ≤80% of area median income, at the SPM-unit level; Urban uses ≤50% AMI at the household level. PolicyEngine's computed housing assistance dollars also under-deliver vs HUD administrative totals, so participation-side comparisons are provisional.

liheap-gap.text: PolicyEngine has LIHEAP only as state fragments (DC, IL, MA, plus TX CEAP and Riverside County) with no national output. National LIHEAP is on the build list.

ccdf-gap.text: PolicyEngine has CCDF only via state child-care subsidy programs and a generic SPM-unit subsidy variable, with no national CCDF coverage. National CCDF is on the build list.

fullpart-flag-list.text: Urban's counterfactual gives every eligible person/household all benefits for which they are eligible (all nine programs). PolicyEngine's headline counterfactual sets every stored take-up flag True plus the WIC gate (exact toggle list recorded in data/pe/pe_meta.json); it cannot add LIHEAP or CCDF (not nationally modeled), and a variant toggling only the six Urban-program flags is also computed to bound the difference.
fullpart-flag-list.basis: Urban slides p.34; data/pe/pe_meta.json runs log; both variants in data/pe/pe_metrics.json

projected-2026.text: The 2026 column ages the same certified artifact to 2026 under current law as encoded in the engine (input uprating; not re-calibrated to 2026 projections). It exists to show what a live model adds over a fixed-vintage report; Urban's tool publishes 2023 only. Attached only where the interchange run's 2024 value matches this pipeline's within 0.5% (same construction); the interchange 2026 full-participation poverty rows are excluded pending the WIC-gate fix (see RECONCILIATION.md).
projected-2026.basis: comparison/ FINDINGS.md '2026 column' section; comparison/RECONCILIATION.md #2; construction gate in pipeline/build_comparison.py

fullpart-headroom.text: The counterfactuals start from structurally different baselines. PolicyEngine's calibrated baseline already places annual participation near administrative levels (e.g. SNAP ≈91% of annual eligibles — see the SNAP participation row), so forcing the remaining flags adds little; Urban's average-month baseline has participation at admin caseload ÷ eligibles (SNAP 57.5%), leaving far more headroom. The two 'full participation' poverty deltas answer different questions until PolicyEngine publishes average-month semantics.
fullpart-headroom.basis: measured in this repo (snap participation_rate row vs Urban's); docs/replication-assessment.md §8; average-month semantics tracked in populace#332

period-participation-semantics.text: PolicyEngine participation is annual-ever (any benefit during 2024) over annual eligibility; Urban's is average-month. Annual-ever rates exceed average-month rates by construction, independent of model quality.

race-construction.text: PolicyEngine race categories come from the artifact's stored race variable (categories recorded in data/pe/pe_meta.json); Urban uses ACS-based non-Hispanic groupings with AAPI including Pacific Islanders. Category construction differs; treat subgroup deltas as indicative.

disability-construction.text: Urban's disability subgroups use the ACS disability questions; PolicyEngine's is_disabled definition is recorded from engine metadata in data/pe/pe_meta.json. The constructions differ.

locale-gap.text: The Populace artifact carries no metro/non-metro flag; metro-status subgroups are not yet computable.

subgroup-not-computed.text: Earner-presence and citizenship subgroups are computable from the artifact but not yet included in the scorecard pipeline (v1 backlog).
